optimizedContext.value:
# HookRunner Port

## Rules

- Declare TypeScript `interface HookRunner`; single `run` method. No abstract class.
- `run(command: string, variables: HookVariables, progressCallback?)` MUST return `Promise<HookResult>`.
- With callback, report progress before subprocess exits: stdout activity, stderr activity, and liveness during output silence. Preserve stdout/stderr identity. Multiple updates allowed; final result unchanged.
- Before execution, expand every `{{key.path}}` by dot-path traversal of `variables`. Preserve token when path unknown, value complex, or unsupported.
- Substitute only string, number, boolean values; shell-escape every substituted value.
- `run` MUST always resolve, never reject. `HookResult`: `exitCode()`, complete `stdout()`, complete `stderr()`, `isSuccess()` true iff exit code 0. Progress MUST NOT replace/weaken captured final result.
- `HookVariables.change?`: `{ name: string; workspace: string; path: string }`; absent without active change. `HookVariables.project`: `{ root: string }`, absolute git-root path.
- Execute deterministic shell `run:` hooks only. MUST NOT handle/interpret `instruction:` hooks or externally dispatched hook backends; external hooks use separate runner abstraction, dispatch rules, accepted-type declaration.
- Caller lifecycle guarantees: non-zero `pre-*` aborts operation; CLI-owned operations run `post-*` before return; agent-driven `post-*` unsupported through `run:` and use `instruction:`.

## Constraints

- Port lives under `application/ports/`; no `child_process`, shell detection, platform process streaming, or I/O dependency.
- Port module re-exports domain value objects `HookResult` and `HookVariables`.
- Subprocess failures become `HookResult`, never thrown exceptions.
- Progress callbacks observational only; MUST NOT alter success/failure semantics or final captured results.
